*Deliverables are answered at the bottom.*
**Access Control Lab Part 1**

**Objective:**

In this activity, you will get some practical experience with Network Access Control, File-level Access Control, and Remote Access Control.

**Instructions:**

1. **Enabling Windows Firewall Logs**

	In order to see all of the activity from the actions we are taking, we need to enable Windows Firewall logs.

2. Open “**Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security**” by searching for it in the Windows search bar. Open as administrator.

   3. Right click on the top most item in the left pain (Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security) and select properties. On **each** profile (Domain, Private, and Public), select “**Customize**” to configure the logging. Use the following settings:

      * **Log dropped packets:** Yes

      * **Log  successful connections:** Yes

      * The rest of the settings can remain. It may be helpful to note where these logs are stored.

4. **Enabling Windows IIS**

You will enable Windows IIS through Windows features, as well as create and access hosted webpages.

1. Open “**Windows Control Panel**” by searching for it in the windows search bar. Click either “**programs**” or “**programs and features**,” then, “**Turn Windows features on or off**,” where you can enable IIS. 

   * If you are getting hung up by a never ending “searching for required files”, use the following commands **as administrator** in **cmd**.

![][image1]

```
taskkill /im TiWorker.exe /f net stop wuauserv /y rmdir "%systemroot%\SoftwareDistribution\Download" /s /q del "%ALLUSERSPROFILE%\Application Data\Microsoft\Network\Downloader\qmgr*.dat" /s /f /q cleanmgr /sageset:65535 & cleanmgr /sagerun:65535 ​Dism /Online /Enable-Feature /FeatureName:NetFx3 /All
```

![][image2]

2. Start up a browser and enter localhost in the URL. You should get the generic splash page for Windows Internet Information Service (IIS). If you ever want to test changes, then use this as a quick spot check.

3. In order to make sure we know which computers and web servers you are dealing with, create a personal page. 

4. Copy the following into notepad:

   \<html\>  
   \<body bgcolor="33bb77"\>

   This is *FirstName Lastname*’s web page … sweet\!

   \</body\>

   \</html\>

5. Save it to “C:\\inetpub\\wwwroot” as “web1.html” 

   * If it says access denied, add permissions on the wwwroot folder (Pro Tip: This is access control in action\!) 🡪 Right-click on folder, Properties, add your user if not there, and give full permission for that user. \#SharingIsCaring

![][image3]

6. Test it out by entering localhost/web1.html. You should see your web page.

7. Now check connectivity to neighbor’s pages by browsing for http://**TheirActualIPaddressHere**/web1.html.

8. **Deliverable 1:** Enter and see if you get their page. 

* *(Take a [**Snip**](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/tutorials/how-to-use-the-windows-snipping-tool/) of a successful connection)*

* *If you don’t, troubleshoot a bit & figure out what might be the main suspects.*

3. **Network Access Control**

You will use a firewall to get some experience and gain some understanding of the concepts by blocking some hosts and services.

1. Open Windows Firewall, and go to Advanced Settings

2. First, you need to disable a pre-defined rule set up to allow all traffic in for IIS. Look at the firewall rules. Find the one labelled World Wide Web Services (HTTP Traffic-IN) and disable it.

3. Create a new **inbound** rule to block the use of port 80 and 443 on your system.

* *Select “**New rule**,” “**port**” enter port 80 and 443, “**block the connection**,” block for domain, private, and public, then name the rule “HTTP” before clicking finish.*

4. **Deliverable 2:** Attempt to connect to a neighbor’s website page again. This time, the port 80 rule should block it.  

* *(Take a [**Snip**](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/tutorials/how-to-use-the-windows-snipping-tool/) of an unsuccessful connection)*

5. Remove your firewall rule, and re-enable the Predefined HTTP rule.

6. Make sure your web traffic works again.

* *Common Troubleshoot Suspects*: check permissions, check file type, check rules, check firewall, check services, check IP addresses, check syntax. 

4. **File Level Access Control**

5. Do this part in groups. All computers should create access rights for other group members.

6. On the Windows 10 virtual machine, create users: 

* *Create a user for yourself*

* *Create a user for neighbor1*

* *Create a user for neighbor2*

**I created three users "Gavin", "Jack", and "Ronan"**

3. Now create a folder under C:\\ called “CyberTest”

4. For that folder, set the names and permissions as given below:

* *Neighbor1 (use name) read only* **Jack**

* *Neighbor 2 (use name) read and write* **Ronan**

**I gave Jack read only access, Ronan read and write access, and Gavin full control.**

  Create a document named “SuperSecretPasswordList.txt”, and save it in the folder.

5.  In order for your neighbors to access the files, enable remote access.

6. Neighbors should launch the Remote Desktop app.

7. Enter the IP address of the Win10 VM.

8. One neighbor should log in with the Neighbor1 account, and another should log in with the Neighbor2 account. Both accounts should then be used to attempt to edit the document 

   9. If you get “the connection was denied because the user account is not authorized” error when users try to remote desktop: On the center machine \-\> Control Panel \-\> System and Security \-\> Under System “Allow Remote Access” \-\> Add user account
	- **We all got this error because we didn't put passwords on the user accounts. Adding passwords solved it.**

11. **Deliverable 3:** Show the instructor that this worked. 

* *Take a snip of the result when Neighbor 1 edits (or attempts to edit) the file.*

* *Take a snip of the result when Neighbor 2 edits (or attempts to edit) the file.* 

10. **Deliverable 4:** *Answer the following questions based on your experience in this lab:*

* *Why is it important to have multiple layers of access instead of relying on just one? Give a specific example from the lab.*

* *When you blocked your neighbor's web access with the firewall, it was very secure… but they couldn't access your website at all. In a real business, you need to balance security with legitimate access. Describe one scenario where you might need to allow access through a firewall while still maintaining security.*

* *Imagine you accidentally gave a user "Full Control" permissions instead of "Read Only" on a folder containing sensitive company financial data. What could go wrong? What would be the potential consequences?*

* *You created user accounts with "simple passwords for sharing purposes" in this lab. Why would this be a terrible idea in a real production environment? What should you do instead?*

* *Think about a website or online service you use regularly. Identify at least TWO types of access control that service probably uses to protect your data. Be specific.*

## 4: Answer the following questions based on your experience in this lab:

* Why is it important to have multiple layers of access control instead of relying on just one? Give a specific example from the lab.
	* **It is important to have multiple layers of access control to prevent a single compromise of a single layer from gaining access to the entire system. If an outer layer becomes compromised there should always be another layer behind it to fall back to. Multiple layers of access control forces an attacker to work much harder and spend much more time than they otherwise would have.**
* When you blocked your neighbor's web access with the firewall, it was very secure… but they couldn't access your website at all. In a real business, you need to balance security with legitimate access. Describe one scenario where you might need to allow access through a firewall while still maintaining security.
	* **One reason you might need to allow access through a firewall is to allow employees at a buisness remote access to a fileserver on the office.**
* Imagine you accidentally gave a user "Full Control" permissions instead of "Read Only" on a folder containing sensitive company financial data. What could go wrong? What would be the potential consequences?
	* **The user with "Full Control" could modify or delete the financial data which would cause huge issues for the integrity and availibility of the data. It could also allow the employee to fly under the radar while stealing money from the company.**
* You created user accounts with "simple passwords for sharing purposes" in this lab. Why would this be a terrible idea in a real production environment? What should you do instead?
	* **In a real production enviroment,  using simple passwords for wasy sharing would be a horrible idea because using an insecure password makes the account it is asociated with very vulnurable. If the password is simple or easily guessable then there might as well not be a password there at all.**
* Think about a website or online service you use regularly. Identify at least TWO types of access control that service probably uses to protect your data. Be specific.
	* **Google drive uses DAC and MAC to protect my data. DAC is used when a file or document is shared with someone, it allows them access because i decided they could have it. MAC is used for all accounts. Nobody can see any data unless they login to an account, and when they are logged into their account they can only see data they own or data that was shared with them.**
